newsitem.title: USA: FBI cuts number identified in Olympic bomb picture.
newsitem.headline: FBI cuts number identified in Olympic bomb picture.

text.p: The FBI Saturday retracted an initial claim it had identified seven of nine people wanted for questioning in the investigation into last summer's Olympic park bombing.

Three of the seven, including one wearing a Green Bay Packers' "cheesehead" booster hat, were pictured near a sound and light tower in Centennial Olympic Park, where the bomb exploded early July 27, 1996, during a crowded outdoor concert.
But the FBI said the three people who came forward to identify themselves as being in the picture were not in the park at the time it was taken.
"That's not the right group of people," FBI spokesman Jay Spadafore said.
"One of the individuals is convinced he was in the photograph, and still is convinced. But we know when it was taken and they just weren't in the park at the right time."

FBI officials initially were elated to think they had identified seven of the nine within 12 hours of a news conference at which they released five images, including photographs, videotape still frames and a composite drawing.
The new information reduced the number of those identified from seven to four.
Federal officials stressed the people pictured were not suspects but simply wanted for questioning in case they had information that could lead investigators to the bomber.
All nine had been seen in the vicinity of a sound and light tower Centennial Olympic Park between 12:15 and 12:45 a.m., when the FBI said the bomb was set in place.

The device was concealed in a military-style backpack and left beneath a green wooden bench at the base of the tower. It exploded at 1:20 a.m., leaving two people dead and injuring Investigators also were still trying to pin down the identities of two lone men.
One blurry figure in an enhanced photograph, described as a man with short dark hair, was pictured standing at the base of the tower with a backpack hanging from his shoulders.

The second man, shown in a composite drawing with a goatee, was seen by several people sitting on the bench sometime after 12:30 a.m. He was described as being in his 20s, standing nearly 6 feet tall and weighing between 140 and 170 pounds.
